capabilities: Plans design, architecture, and infrastructure changes
useCases: Developers who want a written plan before tackling a big change
Students structuring a feature or refactor instead of diving in blind
howTo: Install the skill: npx skills add https://github.com/github/awesome-copilot --skill create-implementation-plan
Describe the feature, refactor, upgrade, or change you are planning
Let it draft the implementation plan file
Review and refine the plan
Use the plan to guide your work
goodToKnow: It produces a plan document, not the implementation itself.
The plan is only as detailed as the context you give it.

skill/harness-writing.tagline: Write effective fuzzing harnesses in any language
skill/harness-writing.overview: This skill shares techniques for writing effective fuzzing harnesses across different languages. It is useful when you are creating new fuzz targets or improving existing harness code.
capabilities: Teaches techniques for writing fuzzing harnesses
useCases: Security engineers adding fuzzing to a project
Students learning how to build fuzz targets for the first time
howTo: Install the skill: npx skills add https://github.com/trailofbits/skills --skill harness-writing
Describe the code or function you want to fuzz
Follow its techniques to write a harness
Hook the harness into your fuzzing tool
Refine the harness to improve coverage
goodToKnow: It covers harness-writing technique, not a specific fuzzing engine.
You still need a fuzzer to actually run the harness.

skill/lark-drive.tagline: Manage Lark (Feishu) Drive files and folders
skill/lark-drive.overview: This skill manages files and folders in Lark (Feishu) Drive. It covers upload and download, creating folders, copy, move, and delete, plus metadata, comments, permissions, subscriptions, and versions. It can also import Word, Markdown, Excel, CSV, PPTX, or .base files into Lark formats. Document content, sheet data, and wiki nodes are handled by separate Lark skills.
capabilities: Uploads, downloads, and organizes Drive files and folders
Manages metadata, comments, permissions, and subscriptions
Imports Word, Markdown, Excel, CSV, PPTX, and .base files into Lark formats
useCases: A Lark user automating file organization and sharing in Drive
Someone importing existing documents into Lark formats
howTo: Install the skill with: npx skills add https://github.com/larksuite/cli --skill lark-drive
Authenticate with your Lark (Feishu) account
Ask it to upload, organize, or import the files you need
Adjust permissions or versions on Drive items as required
goodToKnow: Document content, sheet data, and wiki nodes are handled by separate Lark skills, not this one.
You need a Lark (Feishu) account with appropriate Drive permissions.

skill/customs-trade-compliance.tagline: Customs paperwork and duty optimization help
skill/customs-trade-compliance.overview: This skill helps with the documentation and rules behind international trade. It covers HS tariff classification, Incoterms, using free-trade agreements, and screening restricted parties. It can also help optimize duties and mitigate penalties across different jurisdictions.
capabilities: Classify goods with HS codes for tariffs
Use free-trade agreements where they apply
useCases: A small business owner shipping products internationally who needs correct customs paperwork
Anyone trying to lower duty costs legally or avoid penalties across jurisdictions
howTo: Install the skill with: npx skills add https://github.com/affaan-m/everything-claude-code --skill customs-trade-compliance
Describe the goods you are shipping and the countries involved
Ask for the HS classification and applicable Incoterms
Check whether a free-trade agreement reduces your duties
Run restricted-party screening before finalizing the shipment
goodToKnow: Customs rules vary by country, so always confirm against official sources before shipping.
This is guidance, not legal advice; final compliance is your responsibility.

skill/documentation-2.overview: This skill writes and maintains technical documentation including READMEs, runbooks, onboarding guides, API docs, and architecture docs. It helps you produce clear docs and keep them up to date. Use it whenever your project needs better documentation.
useCases: Developers writing a README or API docs for a project
Teams keeping runbooks and onboarding guides current
howTo: Install the skill with: npx skills add https://github.com/anthropics/knowledge-work-plugins --skill documentation
Point it at the project or feature to document
Choose the doc type, such as a README or API doc
Let it draft the documentation
Review and keep it updated as the project changes
goodToKnow: Covers several doc types, so tell it which one you need.
Review drafts for accuracy against your actual code.

skill/marketing-ideas-3.overview: This skill lets you browse 140 marketing and growth approaches organized by category for promoting a SaaS or software product. It's a structured idea bank you can pull from when you need fresh promotion tactics. It's useful when you're stuck on how to grow a product and want a categorized list to spark ideas.
capabilities: Focus on SaaS and software promotion
useCases: A founder looking for new ways to promote a SaaS product
A marketer building a growth experiment backlog
A student studying common software marketing tactics
howTo: Install the skill with: npx skills add https://github.com/davila7/claude-code-templates --skill marketing-ideas
Browse the approaches by category
Pick tactics that fit your product and audience
Turn the chosen ideas into a marketing plan
goodToKnow: It is an idea bank, not a done-for-you campaign.
Approaches are geared toward SaaS and software products.

skill/async-io-model.tagline: Async IO patterns in the Turso core
skill/async-io-model.overview: This skill explains the asynchronous patterns used in the Turso database core. It covers IOResult, state machines, re-entrancy pitfalls, and CompletionGroup, which you should follow when writing any IO code. It's useful when contributing to Turso and you need to get the async model right.
useCases: A contributor writing IO code in the Turso core
A developer learning Turso's async model
Anyone avoiding re-entrancy pitfalls in Turso IO
howTo: Install the skill with: npx skills add https://github.com/tursodatabase/turso --skill async-io-model
Review the async patterns: IOResult, state machines, and CompletionGroup
Follow these patterns when writing IO code in Turso
Watch for re-entrancy pitfalls the skill describes
goodToKnow: This is specific to the Turso database core's internals.
It is most useful for contributors to that codebase.

skill/pinia-best-practices.tagline: Pinia state management best practices for Vue
skill/pinia-best-practices.overview: This skill shares best practices and common gotchas for Pinia state management in Vue. It covers store setup, reactivity, and pitfalls like reactivity breaking when you destructure from a store. It helps you avoid the traps that quietly break state in Vue apps.
capabilities: Best practices for Pinia state management
Warns about pitfalls like broken reactivity from destructuring
useCases: A Vue developer setting up Pinia stores correctly
Someone debugging reactivity that broke after destructuring a store
howTo: Install it with: npx skills add https://github.com/hyf0/vue-skills --skill pinia-best-practices
Ask the skill about your Pinia store setup or reactivity issue
Apply the recommended patterns
Avoid the noted gotchas like destructuring that breaks reactivity
goodToKnow: It is specific to Pinia and Vue's reactivity model.
Watching out for the destructuring pitfall is a key part of the guidance.

skill/ios-development.tagline: iOS development guidance, end to end
skill/ios-development.overview: This skill provides iOS development guidance covering Swift best practices and SwiftUI patterns. It also helps with UI/UX review against Apple's Human Interface Guidelines, accessibility audits, and planning new apps. It's a broad companion for building iOS apps the Apple way.
capabilities: Apply Swift best practices and SwiftUI patterns
Review UI/UX against Apple's Human Interface Guidelines
useCases: An iOS developer who wants Swift and SwiftUI guidance while building
Someone planning a new app or auditing one for accessibility and HIG compliance
howTo: Install the skill with: npx skills add https://github.com/rshankras/claude-code-apple-skills --skill ios-development
Describe the app or screen you're working on
Ask for Swift or SwiftUI patterns
Request a HIG or accessibility review
Apply the feedback to your code
goodToKnow: It's focused on the Apple platform with Swift and SwiftUI.
You'll still need Xcode and a Mac to build and run iOS apps.

skill/mcp-integration-3.tagline: Add MCP servers to Claude Code plugins
skill/mcp-integration-3.overview: This skill guides you through adding Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers to Claude Code plugins via a .mcp.json file. It covers SSE, stdio, HTTP, and WebSocket server types and the CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT variable. Use it when you want to wire an MCP server into a plugin.
capabilities: Adds MCP servers to Claude Code plugins via .mcp.json
Covers SSE, stdio, HTTP, and WebSocket server types
useCases: A student adding a custom MCP server to a Claude Code plugin
Someone choosing between stdio, SSE, HTTP, or WebSocket transports for an MCP server
howTo: Install the skill with: npx skills add https://github.com/davila7/claude-code-templates --skill mcp-integration
Create or open the .mcp.json file in your plugin
Add your MCP server entry using the right server type (SSE, stdio, HTTP, or WebSocket)
Use CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT where needed and test the connection
goodToKnow: This is specific to Claude Code plugins and the .mcp.json format.
Pick the server type that matches how your MCP server actually runs.

skill/narrative-text-visualization.tagline: Turn data into annotated narrative reports

capabilities: Turns data into structured narrative reports
Annotates key entities so insights stand out
useCases: A student writing a data summary and wanting key numbers highlighted
Someone turning analysis results into a readable narrative report
howTo: Install the skill with: npx skills add https://github.com/antvis/chart-visualization-skills --skill narrative-text-visualization
Provide the data or findings you want summarized
Use the skill to generate a narrative report in T8 syntax
Review the annotated entities to confirm the right insights stand out
goodToKnow: Output uses AntV's T8 syntax, so you may need T8-compatible tooling to render it fully.
The narrative is only as accurate as the data you provide.
